observations: The three TryReadMore loops are the same shape with three different thresholds (7, 11, header_size + length) and share the two exits: TryReadMore false writes its code to *fragment_type_or_err and returns false; TryReadMore true with no buffer growth returns false WITHOUT writing *fragment_type_or_err (the caller then returns 0 -- see the caller disassembly at 0x5f03430). The no-progress arm is the only path that leaves the out-param untouched.

Unlike ReadPhysicalRecord there is NO kBadRecordLen arm: a short body keeps refilling through TryReadMore. kBadRecordLen (14) is in the enum but unreachable from this routine -- the only way the caller sees 14 is via ReadPhysicalRecord.

The recyclable test uses the SIGNED type byte: sub eax,0x5; cmp eax,0x3; ja -- type in 5..8 takes the recyclable arm; a type byte >= 0x80 (negative when sign-extended) takes the plain arm and returns sign-extended (0xFFFFFF80 for 0x80). The zero check (or eax,[rsp+0x1c]) is also on the signed type, so it only fires for byte 0.

The log_num gate fires before the CRC check: a corrupted log_num byte returns kOldRecord (13) even though the CRC is also wrong (bytes 7..10 are inside the CRC coverage). The CRC coverage of the log_num field is therefore not separately observable through the return code.

The CRC covers header+6 .. header_size+length-6 -- the type byte, the recyclable log_num, and the payload -- but NOT the stored CRC or the length. The stored value is masked; the binary unmasks with (stored - 0xa282ead8) rol 15, the exact inverse of Mask.

The decompress loop passes the ORIGINAL length on every Uncompress call (rdx = rbp each iteration) while the input goes null after the first call -- the null-input resume rule from #5972. The loop exits only when remaining == 0 AND produced != kBlockSize, so a full 0x8000-byte output forces another call even with nothing left.

Only type 9 (kSetCompressionType) bypasses decompression in this binary. A newer upstream log_reader.cc also bypasses kUserDefinedTimestampSizeType and kRecyclableUserDefinedTimestampSizeType, but this FDE contains no comparison against those type values, so types 10/11 are decompressed when uncompress_ is set -- the binary is the authority; the packet pins that and records the newer-source difference as an observation, not a model error.

On the Uncompress-error arm the binary clears buffer_ and returns kBadRecord but does NOT write *fragment: the partial uncompressed_record_ stays in the reader and is only overwritten by the next decompress entry. The case ledger records uncompressed_record_after for that arm.

buffer_.clear() never writes drop_size on the zero-record and decompress-error paths (only the kBadRecordChecksum path sets *drop_size = buffer_.size() first, and TryReadMore's own kBadHeader failure is the only way *drop_size is set on the refill paths).

Live engine check: pure-Python CRC32C reproduces the standard 0xE3069283 vector for '123456789' and Mask/Unmask round-trip; a real ZSTD frame wrapped in a real WAL record (type 1, correct masked CRC) runs through the model with the real Uncompress shim and returns True with fragment_type 1 and the original payload; the same frame with uncompress_ absent returns the frame bytes untouched; the same frame as a recyclable type-5 record with a matching log_num returns True with fragment_type 5, the original payload, and recycled_ set.
